question: What is the least possible number which must be subtracted from 16, 19 and 23, so that the resulting numbers are in continued proportion?
solution:
**Given:**

The least possible number which must be subtracted from 16, 19 and 23

**Calculation:**

Let the least possible number which must be subtracted from 16, 19 and 23, so that the resulting numbers are in continued proportion be k

Then,

⇒ (16 – k)/(19 – k) = (19 – k)/(23 – k)

Applying componendo and dividendo

⇒ (16 – k + 19 – k)/(16 – k – 19 – k) = (19 – k + 23 – k)/(19 – k – 23 – k)

⇒ (35 – 2k)/(16 – k – 19 + k) = (42 – 2k)/(19 – k – 23 – k)

⇒ (35 – 2k)/(16 – 19) = (42 – 2k)/(19 – 23)

⇒ (35 – 2k)/(-3) = (42 – 2k)/(-4)

⇒ (35 × 4 – 8k) = (42 × 3 – 6k)

⇒ 140 – 8k = 126 – 6k

⇒ 14 = 2k

⇒ k = 7

**∴ The least number is 7**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Question can be directly solved by putting the option

⇒ 16 : 19 : : 19 : 23

Put option (2)

⇒ (16 – 7) : (19 – 7) : : (19 – 7) : (23 – 7)

⇒ 9 : 12 : : 12 : 16

⇒ 9/12 = 12/16

⇒ b² = ac = (12 × 12) = (9 × 16)

⇒ 144 = 144

**∴ The least possible value is 7**
